kernel.d: A function that runs on the GPU across thousands of threads at once. The CPU doesn't execute it: it only asks the driver to enqueue it on a stream.

cuda-stream.d: A FIFO queue of GPU work. Operations on the same stream execute in order; the CPU enqueues asynchronously and moves on without waiting.

modo-eager.d: Execution one operation at a time: Python reaches a line, PyTorch picks the kernel and the CPU launches it right away. In vLLM: --enforce-eager or cudagraph_mode: NONE.

captura-de-stream.d: A mode in which the operations enqueued on a stream are recorded into a graph instead of executed (cudaStreamBeginCapture → cudaStreamEndCapture). Nothing runs during capture.

replay.d: Re-execution of an instantiated CUDA graph (cudaGraphLaunch): a single CPU call fires every recorded kernel, which reads and writes exactly the same memory addresses as during capture.

buffer-estatico.d: A fixed-address tensor used as the input or output of a CUDA graph. Before each replay, the new data is copied into it; the tensor itself is never swapped.

tamanhos-de-captura.d: The list of batch sizes (in tokens) for which vLLM records a CUDA graph. A smaller batch is padded up to the next size in the list; one larger than the last size runs eager.

padding-de-lote.d: Filling a batch with dummy rows up to the nearest captured size. The work on those rows is wasted, and they must be masked so they don't write to the wrong place.

decode-uniforme.d: A step in which every request has the same number of query tokens: 1 without speculation, or k+1 when each one verifies k drafts. It is the case FULL graphs cover.

linhas-de-verificacao.d: The number of tokens in a speculative decode step: sequences × (k+1). In DS, 6 × 7 = 42; it determines which capture sizes are needed.

decodificacao-especulativa.d: A cheap drafter proposes k tokens and the large model verifies them all in a single step, accepting the longest correct prefix. Covered in detail in Part VII.

piecewise.d: A mode in which the forward is split at the attention operations: the pieces between them become CUDA graphs and attention runs eager between one piece and the next. Requires torch.compile's piecewise compilation.

full-graph.d: A CUDA graph that covers the entire forward, attention included. It requires attention metadata in persistent buffers and, in many backends, a uniform batch.

breakable-cudagraph.d: A vLLM variant in which marked functions break the capture at capture time: they close the segment, run eager on the stream and open a new segment, without depending on piecewise compilation. DS and Qwen (v0.30 lane) turn it off with VLLM_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDAGRAPH=0; GLM doesn't set the variable.

batch-descriptor.d: The key vLLM's dispatcher uses to choose which CUDA graph to play in a step: number of tokens, number of requests, whether the batch is uniform and whether LoRA is present.

torch-compile.d: PyTorch's compiler: Dynamo captures the forward as an FX graph and Inductor generates fused kernels (Triton). In vLLM it is controlled by --compilation-config (mode 0 to 3).

dynamo.d: The part of torch.compile that intercepts Python bytecode and records the tensor operations into an FX graph, together with guards (conditions under which the graph remains valid).

inductor.d: The torch.compile backend that turns the FX graph into optimized code, fusing neighboring operations (add, norm, activation) into a single Triton kernel.

grafo-fx.d: PyTorch's representation of a program as a list of nodes (operations) connected by the tensors flowing between them; it is what torch.compile analyzes and rewrites.

custom-op.d: An operation registered in torch.library (in vLLM, via direct_register_custom_op, and called as torch.ops.vllm.name) that the compiler treats as a black box.

fake-impl.d: The “pretend” implementation of a custom op: it computes nothing, it only returns tensors with the right shape and dtype so the compiler can propagate shapes through the graph.

mutates-args.d: The list of arguments a custom op writes in place. It tells the compiler not to reorder, duplicate or eliminate those writes.

async-scheduling.d: A vLLM mode in which the scheduler prepares step N+1 while the GPU executes step N, hiding the CPU cost of scheduling (but not that of the launches inside the step).

jit.d: Compiling a kernel the first time it is called with a given key (constants, dtypes, alignments), rather than at install time. Triton, TileLang, CuTeDSL, DeepGEMM and FlashInfer all work this way.

constexpr.d: A Triton kernel parameter known at compile time. Each distinct value produces a distinct binary (and dead branches are eliminated).

cache-de-jit.d: The directory where a JIT compiler stores the binaries it has already generated (TRITON_CACHE_DIR, TILELANG_CACHE_DIR, ~/.nv/ComputeCache…). If it dies every time the container is recreated, everything recompiles.

bucket.d: A range of sizes rounded up (e.g., to the next power of 2) so that many real sizes share the same compiled kernel.

warmup.d: Synthetic runs at boot that force JIT compilations, allocations and autotunes to happen before real traffic arrives.

autotune.d: Benchmarking several tactics of a kernel (tile size, split-K, stages) for a given shape and storing the fastest one in a cache. It must happen before capture and be consistent across ranks.

rank.d: Each process in a distributed group — here, one GPU in one node. Rank 0 is usually the leader.

all-reduce.d: A collective in which every rank contributes a tensor, the tensors are summed and every rank receives the result. All of them must call the same collective, with the same size, in the same order.

watchdog-nccl.d: A thread in PyTorch's ProcessGroupNCCL that kills the process if a collective doesn't finish within the deadline (600 s by default).

ima.d: A CUDA error for accessing an invalid address; it usually brings the process down. In the recipes it shows up as a symptom of corrupted indices or slots.

canario.d: An automatic post-boot test that checks whether the engine responds sensibly (e.g., “OK” at temperature 0 and accepted drafts) before declaring the service ready.

rodada-de-decode.d: TensorFold's unit of decode work: each stream proposes drafts, a single forward verifies the window [pending token, drafts…], each row is sampled with the request's key, drafts are accepted up to the first disagreement and the accepted rows are committed.

janela-de-verificacao.d: The rows a verification forward processes: the pending token plus one stream's drafts (up to 16 rows in TensorFold) or several streams' drafts side by side (up to 32 in v1.3.2; 16 to 64 since v1.5, with TF_GLM_MULTI_WINDOW). In TensorFold, each window width has its own CUDA graph.

tabela-no-device.d: A GPU tensor holding the metadata that changes every step (position, extent base, slot, parity, bounds). The graph records the table's address; the host rewrites its contents in place before each replay and the kernels read them, so one graph serves any mix of streams.

paridade-dupla.d: Each slot keeps its recurrent state in two copies: the verify window reads one and writes the other. If every draft is accepted, the parity flips; otherwise the state is recomputed from the kept rows only (replay).

epoca-no-device.d: An exchange counter kept in GPU memory and advanced by the kernel itself (the last block to finish). Because it is not an argument passed by the CPU, each replay of a CUDA graph uses the next number — this is how TensorFold's RDMA all-gather survives replay.
